result.instructions: Tools for Jenkins, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Which of our jobs failed in the last 24 hours?"; "Show me the end of the log for the last failed build of deploy-prod."; "What is waiting in the build queue, and is any agent offline?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Jenkins data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run jenkins_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run jenkins_request_feature to record the request. Paid plans: Pro (10,000 tool calls a month, $9/month or $90/year, for normal use) and Pro+ (100,000 tool calls a month, $39/month or $390/year, for automations and heavy use). A plan can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run jenkins_upgrade without a plan: it returns both plans, each with a payment link for the user to open. jenkins_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: jenkins_get_server
tools.title: Get server info
tools.description: Get the Jenkins controller summary: mode, description, executor count, whether it is quieting down (shutting down for restart), and whether security is on. Jenkins API: GET /api/json.

tools.name: jenkins_list_jobs
tools.title: List jobs
tools.description: List the jobs at the top level, or inside a folder, with their status colour (blue = success, red = failed, yellow = unstable, grey = never built, *_anime = running). Jenkins API: GET /api/json or /job/<folder>/api/json.

folder.description: Folder path, for example team/backend. Leave empty for the top level.

tools.name: jenkins_get_job
tools.title: Get a job
tools.description: Get one job: buildable state, next build number, health score, last build, last successful and failed builds, and the parameters a build can take. Jenkins API: GET /job/<path>/api/json.

job.description: Job name, or folder/job for a job inside a folder (for example team/backend/deploy-prod).

tools.name: jenkins_list_builds
tools.title: List builds
tools.description: List the most recent builds of a job, newest first, with result (SUCCESS, FAILURE, UNSTABLE, ABORTED, or null while running), timing and display name. Jenkins API: GET /job/<path>/api/json with a builds range.

job.description: Job name, or folder/job for a job inside a folder (for example team/backend/deploy-prod).

limit.description: How many builds to return (default 20, max 100).

tools.name: jenkins_get_build
tools.title: Get a build
tools.description: Get one build: result, timing, what started it, the agent it ran on, and the commits it built (changeSets). Jenkins API: GET /job/<path>/<n>/api/json.

job.description: Job name, or folder/job for a job inside a folder (for example team/backend/deploy-prod).

build.description: Build number (for example 42), or lastBuild, lastSuccessfulBuild, lastFailedBuild, lastCompletedBuild.

tools.name: jenkins_get_build_log
tools.title: Get a build log (tail)
tools.description: Get the end of a build's console log, where the error usually is. Returns the last tail_bytes bytes (default 20000, max 200000) and the total log size. Jenkins API: GET /job/<path>/<n>/logText/progressiveText.

job.description: Job name, or folder/job for a job inside a folder (for example team/backend/deploy-prod).

build.description: Build number (for example 42), or lastBuild, lastSuccessfulBuild, lastFailedBuild, lastCompletedBuild.

tail_bytes.description: Bytes from the end of the log to return (default 20000, max 200000).

tools.name: jenkins_get_queue
tools.title: Get the build queue
tools.description: List the items waiting in the build queue, with why each waits, whether it is blocked or stuck, and which job it will run. Jenkins API: GET /queue/api/json.

tools.name: jenkins_list_nodes
tools.title: List agents (nodes)
tools.description: List the build agents with their executors, labels and state: offline, idle, temporarily offline, and the offline reason. Jenkins API: GET /computer/api/json.

tools.name: jenkins_trigger_build
tools.title: Start a build
tools.description: Queue a new build of a job, with optional string parameters (for example {"ENV": "staging"}). The job runs with its own permissions, so this can deploy or change systems. Returns the queue item URL. Jenkins API: POST /job/<path>/build or /buildWithParameters.

job.description: Job name, or folder/job for a job inside a folder (for example team/backend/deploy-prod).

parameters.description: Build parameters as name → value. Leave empty for a job without parameters.

prompts.name: getting_started
prompts.title: Get started with Jenkins
prompts.description: What you can do with Jenkins here, with example requests to try.

prompts.name: find_failed_builds_and_read_the_error
prompts.title: Find failed builds and read the error
prompts.description: List the recent builds of a job and see which ones failed or were unstable. Open one build and read the end of its console log.

prompts.name: check_the_build_queue_and_the_agents
prompts.title: Check the build queue and the agents
prompts.description: See which items wait in the build queue, and why each one waits. Check which build agents are offline or temporarily unavailable.

prompts.name: review_the_state_of_a_job
prompts.title: Review the state of a job
prompts.description: List the top-level jobs or the jobs in one folder. Read the health, last builds and build parameters of one job.

prompts.name: start_a_build_with_parameters
prompts.title: Start a build with parameters
prompts.description: Queue a new build of a job with optional string parameters, such as an environment name. The job runs with its own permissions and can deploy.
